decision: Treat Granola as a lifecycle reference, not a source-code template
evidence: Granola bundle has separate mic/system buffers, live chunk revisions, local and cloud ASR, diarization, encrypted storage, note generation, consent state, and calendar integration
rationale: The useful product pattern is the durable meeting document and recovery path, while PinDrop must keep an independent open-source implementation

decision: Make Dictate, Voice Note, and Meeting equal top-level product pillars
evidence: PinDrop navigation centers Home, Stats, Library, Notes, Dictionary, and Models; meeting capture is a secondary action and voice-note captures are not linked to their transcript
rationale: The information architecture does not yet express the requested product thesis

decision: Create a shared capture-session domain with distinct modes
evidence: Current flows for dictation, note append, quick capture, and meetings route through AppCoordinator but persist different and weakly linked artifacts
rationale: A common session and artifact model gives reuse without making the three user workflows identical

decision: Preserve microphone and system audio as separate timestamped streams
evidence: Granola keeps separate source buffers and can continue if one source fails; PinDrop mixed capture currently discards real-time buffers and mixes temporary files only at stop
rationale: Source separation enables live transcription, reliable You/Others attribution, independent failure recovery, and later diarization

decision: Fix long-session reliability before adding calendar automation
evidence: PinDrop meeting capture uses a ten-minute ASR byte limit, contiguous Data finalization, required diarization, and batch-only transcription
rationale: A central meeting feature must first survive normal 60 to 90 minute meetings without data loss

decision: Use human notes as anchors and generated notes as a derived artifact
evidence: Granola combines rough notes, transcript, and calendar context, then exposes citations; PinDrop notes and meeting records are currently separate
rationale: This keeps users in control and makes summaries auditable

decision: Make model choice explicit by pipeline stage
evidence: PinDrop already supports several local speech engines and broad BYOM text providers, but generic BYOM speech is incomplete
rationale: Separate Live ASR, Final ASR, diarization, and note-generation assignments preserve privacy and quality choices

decision: Defer calendar detection, auto-start, cross-meeting chat, and virtual-camera consent
evidence: These are Granola capabilities, but PinDrop lacks the reliable session foundation and linked meeting-note domain
rationale: They add reach only after the core capture-to-note loop is trustworthy

decision: Do not modify the PinDrop worktree during this investigation
evidence: The repo is on main, ahead by two commits, with many existing user changes
rationale: The request is for investigation and planning, and preserving the user's dirty worktree is required

decision: Define CaptureSession as an artifact-owning domain, not a coordinator wrapper
evidence: Independent review confirmed that current persistence has only optional note-to-transcript linkage and transcript-level fields
rationale: The domain must own source streams, chunks, revisions, derived notes, provider snapshots, recovery, and failure state to pay for its complexity

decision: Link voice notes before promoting the new information architecture
evidence: Independent review confirmed quick capture saves sourceTranscriptionID as nil and note append delivers only plain text
rationale: The visible three-pillar shell should represent durable product behavior, not only new navigation

decision: Sequence generated meeting notes after capture and artifact reliability
evidence: Independent review challenged placing note generation too early because the current path has a ten-minute cap, one final blob, and required diarization
rationale: Citations and human-note anchors require stable timestamped transcript artifacts first

decision: Persist only committed live voice-note revisions
evidence: Tentative streaming tails can rewrite; the committed-text observer now records microphone-attributed, provider-bound cumulative checkpoints with exact retry and prefix invariants
rationale: Durable revisions must survive a crash without treating unstable decoder text as user data

decision: Defer voice-note recovery delivery until capture intent is durable
evidence: Quick capture has no note target at start, while note-append target identity exists only in AppCoordinator memory
rationale: Startup delivery cannot safely create or append notes until the anchored-note phase persists explicit capture intent and destination
